html:
Panamá Viejo is the ruin of the first Spanish city on the Pacific coast of the Americas, founded by Pedrarias Dávila on 15 August 1519. It was the origin of today's Panama City.

It was the Pacific end of the route across the isthmus. Silver from Potosí and Peru came by ship from Lima, crossed by mule trains and river boats to Portobelo on the Caribbean, and sailed for Spain. Pizarro set out from here to conquer the Inca.

In 1671 the Welsh buccaneer Henry Morgan crossed the isthmus and sacked it, and the city burned. The Spanish rebuilt it a few kilometres away, on a site easier to defend, the old quarter of today's capital of Panama. The ruins, with their cathedral tower, are a World Heritage Site.
sum: Panamá Viejo is the ruin of the first Spanish city on the Pacific coast of the Americas, founded by Pedrarias Dávila on 15 August 1519. It was the origin of today's Panama City.
